body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for Maidenmist Cemetery: 8 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: Rook's own stones and ledger are his Thread's: nobody asks about a grave of his. Do not describe the dead things in the depths. Yorgrim the gravedigger has gone silent: name him only if the facts do.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Rook + Tobin (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, tobin_hayward)
  Story now: The party has come to the bent iron gate of the cemetery, between two hooded reapers.
  In front of them: The Maidenmist Gate: A bent iron gate between two hooded reapers, and a fence that runs off into fog. A fifteen-foot iron picket fence on a stone footing runs into the mist both ways. The gate hangs bent outward between two hooded iron reapers, and a broken chain lies in the mud. Beyond it, cobbles climb into grey. Parts of it: The approach; The gate; Beyond the fence. Things to see: A hooded iron reaper; The bent gate; A snapped iron chain in the mud; The fog, thickening; A lamp the fog has drowned; Iron pickets, cold to the touch; A sunken grave; A headstone with a rhyme nobody finished; A cairn of grave-stones.
EXCHANGE 2: Silas + Delphine (speaker ids: silas_vane, delphine_ravelle)
  Story now: The party is walking the Corpse Road through the mist.
  In front of them: The Corpse Road: Three miles of cobbled hearse road between dense grave markers, in mist at its thickest. The road runs straight and wide enough for a hearse, and every yard of its edge is a grave. The mist sits on it like a lid. Parts of it: The first mile; The second mile; The third mile. Things to see: The first mile: the fog leans on you; The third mile: the cold deepens; A mile marker, worn smooth; A hearse wheel, long since broken; A leaning marker, the name worn away; A scatter of old bones; A dead tree, bent toward the sepulcher; A cairn of grave-stones; A dead tree hung with fog.
EXCHANGE 3: Lucan + Cordelia (speaker ids: lucan_houndstooth, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has taken the shortcut through the endless gravestones. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Endless Gravestones (A): Rolling hills of grave markers a few feet apart, a shortcut that always brings a fight. The markers crowd so close the path is a suggestion. Something is always walking between them. Parts of it: Gravestones, stretch 1; Gravestones, stretch 2; Gravestones, stretch 3; Gravestones, stretch 4. Things to see: A marker with your own name begun on it; A scatter of old bones; A cairn of grave-stones; A leaning marker, the name worn away; A sunken grave; A dead tree, bent toward the sepulcher; A headstone with a rhyme nobody finished; A dead tree hung with fog; A weathered headstone.
EXCHANGE 4: Silas + Lucan (speaker ids: silas_vane, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party is walking the Cremation Gardens, among the urns and fountains. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Cremation Gardens: Brick-paved memorial walks lined with clay urns, a fountain at every circle, purple and white flowers in the rain. Rain falls steadily on the urns and a bell tolls somewhere beyond the hedges. Fountains burble at the walk's circles, and a brazier of purple coals waits beside the middle one. Parts of it: The brazier circle; The urn walks; The path in. Things to see: A brazier of purple coals by the fountain; A wishing fountain; A row of mourning urns; A tall clay urn, humming; A tall clay urn, silent; A bed of lavender; A bed of white lilies; A memorial urn, ash-grey; A memorial plaque in the brick.
EXCHANGE 5: Silas + Cordelia (speaker ids: silas_vane, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party is in the Mausoleum Lanes, among small ivy-grown vaults and murky water.
  In front of them: The Mausoleum Lanes: A boggy city of small ivy-grown vaults, murky water in the tile cracks, a brazier of pink coals at the end of a sunken lane. A fen has crept into the dead city. Water seeps between the tiles, moss hangs from gnarled trees, and every vault door is carved with a ship, a sea or a spiral. Parts of it: The sunken lane; The vault rows; The southern vaults; The acrid muck. Things to see: A brazier of pink coals beside a mossy tree; Acrid muck on the tiles; Vault doors carved with ships and spirals; A vault door with a hex glyph; A small vault, its door ajar; A gnarled tree hung with moss; A sunken vault slab; Ivy over a vault door; A scatter of old bones.
EXCHANGE 6: Delphine + Lucan (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party has come to King's Rest, the great barrow with the armoured king over it. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: King's Rest: An enormous palatial barrow, a giant armoured king raising a sword through the fog, huge rune-covered doors. Past a field of wrecked iron the barrow rises, and on its roof a king of stone lifts a sword into the fog. Wights and shrouded fight at its doors, endlessly, and none of them look over. Parts of it: The approach; The rune doors. Things to see: A giant armoured king, sword raised; Huge doors, rune-covered stone; Wights and shrouded, locked in a war that does not end; Broken iron and older bones.
EXCHANGE 7: Rook + Silas (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, silas_vane)
  Story now: The party has come to the Shadestone Sanctuary, a quiet place among the standing stones.
  In front of them: The Shadestone Sanctuary: Tall carved standing stones covered in Orc names before a small stepped ziggurat, an azure beacon on its crown. The air here is still and clean. Names are cut into the standing stones from root to crown, and an azure fire burns on top of the little ziggurat as if it had never gone out. Parts of it: The standing stones; The ziggurat; The chamber of rest. Things to see: The azure beacon; The standing stones, cut with Orc names; A stone with names in a script you almost know; A slab with a shovel laid across it; A statue of a hooded figure holding a lantern; A stone slab; A standing stone cut with names.
EXCHANGE 8: Rook + Cordelia (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has gone down into the Necropolis Depths. The necrolisk is not yet dealt with.
  In front of them: The Necropolis Depths: A huge cavern widened by claws, tunnels lined with slimed corpses, pockets of glowing Shroud-ooze. The cave smells of wet stone and old meat. Something has dug here for a very long time, and it left its slime on everything. Parts of it: The great cavern; The necrolisk's lair. Things to see: A cracked wall leaking grey mist; A broken cavern, and the smell of something large; A slime blob, trapping something dead; A slimed corpse in a burrow wall.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 8 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 8, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY rook_coldwake: That iron gate is bent outward against regulation, Tobin, and someone snapped the chain straight into the mud. Whatever left this yard did not sign the shift log.
SAY tobin_hayward: Never mind the hinges, Rook, this mud tastes of drowned iron and lazy ditch-digging. Look at that sunken grave by the pickets, collapsing straight into the taproot.
SAY rook_coldwake: Poor subsidence control, though the stone footing along the fence is decent enough work. Mind the turf by that unfinished rhyme, the clay has gone soft.
SAY tobin_hayward: Half a verse carved in stone and the mason didn't even knot the end of the thought. Breathe in, man, your chest hasn't moved since the road.
SAY rook_coldwake: Right, thank you, I had that scheduled for the gatehouse.

EXCHANGE 2
SAY delphine_ravelle: Three miles of hearse ruts and not a single footlight on the cobbles, Silas. If this fog gets any thicker, I will have to bow to the cheap seats by ear.
SAY silas_vane: Easy, friend, just listen to the air rattling through my ribs and keep off the verge. Every yard of this road is a marked deck of old bones.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Look at that broken hearse wheel rotting in the ditch, darling, what a dreadful way to miss curtain. Your Foolishness is trying to rhyme "sepulcher" with "velour" and failing miserably.
SAY silas_vane: Tell him to fold, because the chill past this worn mile marker is biting right into my knuckles. House always wins on a road built for one-way traffic.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Then let us walk faster before the damp takes the starch out of my hem.

EXCHANGE 3
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, the dark has teeth between these markers, Cordelia, and they are crowded in with no regard for spacing. Even Barnaby is keeping his tail tucked near my boots.
SAY cordelia_skein: The spatial ratio is terribly cramped, darling, though the lichen on this weathered headstone has a lovely pathology. Oh, do look, someone has started carving my name into this slab.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, that is a dreadful breach of etiquette, and the lettering posture is three out of ten at best. Step wide of that dead tree, if you please, something is pacing the fog.
SAY cordelia_skein: My pulse hasn't even risen, though I appreciate the mason getting the sibilants in my surname right. It takes a very steady hand to leave a stone half-empty.

EXCHANGE 4
SAY silas_vane: Ten silver says the wishing fountain is rigged, Lucan, and all these little clay urns are just waiting for a sucker to drop a coin. You feel that hum coming off the tall one?
SAY lucan_houndstooth: That is not a wager, friend, it is a resonance, and a rather mournful specimen of pottery at that. Barnaby is staring at the purple coals in that brazier as if somebody dropped kettle corn.
SAY silas_vane: Smart dog, at least the brazier keeps the rain off my censer while that bell tolls the count. Half these urns are dead quiet and the other half won't shut up.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Give the lavender bed its due, Silas, it masks the wet ash with admirable manners. A gentleman does not shake the urns to see who is still inside.
SAY silas_vane: Wasn't gonna shake 'em, friend, just checking the fine print on the brick plaque.

EXCHANGE 5
SAY cordelia_skein: Mind your ankles in the tile cracks, Silas, the viscosity of this fen-muck is positively clinging. Every vault door down the lane carries a spiral or a ship, like a taxonomy of drowning.
SAY silas_vane: Takes me right back to the Kalero river landings, darling, except the landlords here locked the doors from the outside. Look at that little vault sitting ajar with the hex glyph on the lintel.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do hold still, this will only tingle while I take a silk-thread note of those pink coals by the mossy tree. The humours rising off this sunken lane are remarkably acrid.
SAY silas_vane: Sketch fast, because my shadow is lagging a half-step in the water and it hates getting wet. Nobody carves a ship on a stone box unless they expect the tide to come up.

EXCHANGE 6
SAY delphine_ravelle: Now that is proper billing, Lucan, a giant stone king raising his blade right through the soup. Though the extras brawling at his rune doors could use a firmer director.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Prime specimen of royal masonry, I grant you, eight out of ten for sheer theatrical scale. Yet those wights and shrouded have been trading the same sloppy lunge for an age.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Mind the seams, darling, there is broken iron everywhere and none of these fighters are even looking at the house. Why put on a show in the fog if you never take a bow?
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Because the quarry they were set to guard is long cold behind those doors, if you please. Even a loyal hound knows when to lie down after the master is gone.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Well, keep Barnaby by your heel, I have no wish to mend a spectral collar tonight.

EXCHANGE 7
SAY silas_vane: Air's clean here, Rook, no fog pressing on the ribs and that blue fire on the ziggurat burns steady as a lighthouse. What do you make of the shovel laid flat across the slab?
SAY rook_coldwake: Tools down, shift ended, proper and square. Whoever cut these Orc names from root to crown knew how to leave a tidy docket.
SAY silas_vane: Look at the script on this near stone, friend, I can almost read the stake they were marking down. Makes a bloke want to check the chalk tallies inside his own ribs.
SAY rook_coldwake: Settle down now, Silas, a monument isn't a tab to be collected. When a stone is cut this deep, you leave the ledger as it lies and keep watch.
SAY silas_vane: Fair enough, warden, just strange seeing a lantern statue that doesn't make my bones itch.

EXCHANGE 8
SAY rook_coldwake: Gross neglect of subterranean zoning, this, and the walls are leaking grey mist through the cracks. Whatever clawed this burrow out has no respect for load-bearing stone.
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology in the Shroud-ooze, Rook, see how the slime preserves the specimen in the burrow wall? My six eyes are clicking so loud I can barely hear the drips.
SAY rook_coldwake: Keep your vials clear of it, Cordelia, my knuckles are feeling soft enough in this damp without adding cave rot. That smell is old meat and bad drainage.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do not fret, darling, if I let this slime sour my calibration, I would be digging in the dark right alongside it. Let us clear the cavern before the ooze ruins my waistcoat.
